papers.title: AlN/AlGaN heterostructure field-effect transistor power devices advantageous for high-temperature application
papers.summary: We report a high-quality AlN/Al0.73Ga0.27N heterostructure field-effect transistor (HFET) advantageous for high-temperature application. The epitaxial heterostructures exhibit a full width at half maximum of 79 arc sec in the (0002) XRD rocking curve, a surface roughness of 0.35 nm, a room-temperature two-dimensional electron gas density of 1.4 × 1013 cm−2 and mobility of 147 cm2/V/s. Two-terminal mesa breakdown measurements revealed an intrinsic critical electric field of 5.6 MV/cm for a 3 μm gap. AlN/Al0.73Ga0.27N HFET devices with gate–drain spacings of 5, 10, 25, and 50 μm were fabricated, and the breakdown voltages are 990, 1420, 2045, and 4203 V, respectively. Remarkably, the saturated drain current exhibits a positive temperature coefficient, in contrast to the negative coefficient in conventional gallium nitride high-electron-mobility transistors, and the threshold voltage decreases from −9.3 to −7.9 V in the temperature range from 25 to 175 °C. This anomalous behavior is attributed to dominant carrier de-trapping from deep-level traps, confirmed by pulsed I–V measurements, temperature-dependent C–V, and Hall measurements. These observations provide strong evidence for the multi-kilovolt-class and high-temperature power switching applications of the AlN/Al0.73Ga0.27N HFET devices.

papers.title: Depletion-mode N-polar AlN-based high electron mobility transistors on sapphire with improved on/off ratios
papers.summary: We report N-polar AlN-based high electron mobility transistors (HEMTs) with a GaN channel thickness of 5.2 nm on N-polar AlN on sapphire. The threshold voltage is around −3.0 to −2.4 V, with saturation currents over 240 mA/mm and on/off ratios as high as 104, much higher than those of previously reported N-polar AlN-based HEMTs. The improved on/off ratio achieved in this work is attributed to the use of an abrupt AlN/GaN heterostructure with a dedicated AlN transition layer, together with improved gate leakage. Both the high-frequency performance and the on-resistance of ≈20 Ω mm are limited by the 2000 Ω/□ sheet resistance of the channel layer.

papers.title: Frequency improvement and asymmetry characteristics of tri-stripe AlGaN/GaN MSM-2DEG varactors
papers.summary: This study presents an AlGaN/GaN heterojunction varactor employing a tri-stripe metal–semiconductor–metal (MSM) structure that exploits the two-dimensional electron gas (2DEG). The device exhibits a strong dependence of its electrical characteristics on the device width (W): both series resistance and capacitance decrease monotonically with reducing W. Through dimensional scaling, the R0·Cj product of the device decreases significantly, thereby improving the cutoff frequency (fc). Although the capacitance switching ratio (Cratio) shows a slight decrease with reduced W, the overall cutoff frequency figure-of-merit (FOM) of the device is effectively improved. Specifically, using a tri-stripe MSM-2DEG structure with a width of 10 μm and a gate gap of 450 nm, a high FOM of 8.27 THz and a Cratio of 3.42 are obtained. The study further reveals that the capacitance characteristics become asymmetric for smaller W values. Concurrently, the shift voltage (Vshift) shifts toward lower voltages with decreasing W, corresponding to the point of most rapid capacitance change, where the Fermi level (Ef) aligns with the conduction band (Ec) minimum. This phenomenon is closely related to the reduction in 2DEG concentration at the AlGaN/GaN interface, likely attributed to enhanced etching-induced damage during size scaling. The 2DEG concentration vs bias exhibits a transition from linear decay on both sides when Ef is far from Ec minimum, to exponential decay near Vshift region—representing a “linear–exponential–linear” evolution. Furthermore, the fabrication process of the device is significantly simplified—all electrodes can be formed in a single step via electron beam lithography.

papers.title: Nanowire-Assisted Epitaxial Lateral Overgrowth of Planar GaN(0001) on Diamond(100)
papers.summary: GaN-on-diamond heterostructures are promising for high-power and high-frequency electronics, however, direct epi- taxial growth on diamond (100) remains challenging due to severe lattice and thermal mismatches, which induce high threading dislocation densities. To overcome this challenge, we have used Plasma Assisted Molecular Beam Epitaxy (PAMBE) to grow wurtzite GaN layers on diamond(100) substrates using nanowire-assisted epitaxial lateral overgrowth (ELOG). Two nanowire templates (NW100, NW600) were benchmarked against a nanowire-free reference (NW000). High-resolution XRD, φ -scans, (0002) pole figures, and reciprocal space mapping show that NW100 attains the lowest dislocation density (5.51 x 10-4 nm-2) and microstrain (2.736 x 10-3), the narrowest (0002) reflection, and a c-axis lattice parameter (5.1821 Å) within 0.06% of the bulk value; NW000, in contrast, exhibits a contracted c-axis (5.1633 Å) and elevated dislocation density (6.26 x 10-4 nm-2), consistent with residual tensile stress. Cross-sectional TEM con- firms the intended diamond/AlN/nanowire/ELOG/planar-GaN layer sequence and shows threading dislocations bending into near-lateral trajectories, directly evidencing defect filtering by the nanowire template. Together, these results estab- lish nanowire-assisted ELOG as an effective strategy to suppress dislocation propagation and recover near-bulk lattice parameters in GaN-on-diamond heteroepitaxy, providing a structurally well-defined platform for device integration.

papers.title: Artificial gauge field modulated on-chip gigahertz acoustic coupling
papers.summary: Phononic integrated circuits (PhICs) represent a promising paradigm for on-chip acoustic information processing. However, conventional straight-waveguide architectures suffer from intrinsically dispersive inter-waveguide coupling, limiting bandwidth and fabrication tolerance. Meanwhile, evanescent crosstalk between adjacent waveguides fundamentally constrains integration density. Here, we introduce an artificial gauge field (AGF) to suppress inter-waveguide coupling dispersion on a CMOS-compatible GaN-on-4H-SiC platform, as validated by the theoretical and experimental demonstration of a broadband 1:1 power divider (PD). Beyond outperforming conventional straight-waveguide directional couplers in broadband performance, the AGF-modulated PD exhibits enhanced robustness against both global offsets and local waveguide-gap perturbations. We further demonstrate the first realization of acoustic coherent destruction of tunneling, enabling crosstalk-free parallel waveguide arrays for densely integrated phononic architectures. Our work thus marks a significant advance toward scalable, high-density, and fabrication-tolerant PhICs.

papers.title: Self-powered, filter-free, and fast solar-blind photodetectors enabled by luminescent converters with giant Stokes shift
papers.summary: Solar-blind photodetectors (SBPDs) are commonly plagued by trade-offs among superior spectral selectivity, high responsivity, and rapid photoresponse speed. Herein, we report a self-powered SBPD integrated with an Er3+-doped metal halide luminescent converter, nominal composition Cs2Ag0.3Na0.7In0.6Er0.4Cl6, which features an enormous Stokes shift. This luminescent medium converts deep-ultraviolet (DUV) photons into visible emission, which is subsequently captured by a commercial silicon photodiode (Si PD). The converter realizes two integrated functions simultaneously: highly efficient DUV-to-visible photon conversion and intrinsic visible-light rejection, thereby removing the requirement for additional external optical filters. Operated under zero bias, the fabricated device delivers a remarkable responsivity of 226.7 mA/W upon 280 nm irradiation at an optical power of 10 μW, an eightfold enhancement relative to the pristine Si PD. Meanwhile, the photodetector exhibits a prominent photo-to-dark current ratio of approximately 4500. More importantly, the system exhibits an ultrafast photoresponse, with rise and fall times measured at 143 and 77 μs, respectively, which is about three orders of magnitude faster than typical Ga2O3-based SBPDs limited by persistent photoconductivity. The proposed design circumvents the intrinsic material drawbacks of conventional wide-bandgap semiconductors, establishing a strategy for low-cost, high-speed solar-blind photodetection.

papers.title: Hydrogen Ion-Cut Single-Crystal Diamond Membranes for Wide and Ultrawide Bandgap Semiconductor Heterointegration
papers.summary: Single-crystal diamond membranes (SCDms) were created using a hydrogen ion-cut process combined with a two-step post-implantation annealing, electrochemical etching, and micro-transfer printing. Monte Carlo simulations comparing H, He, C, and O implantation predicted a narrower vacancy-distribution profile for hydrogen under the implantation conditions examined. Raman spectroscopy was used to evaluate implantation-induced lattice damage and its recovery during annealing and membrane release, while optical bandgap analysis provided further evidence of restoration of the diamond lattice structure. After delamination and removal of residual graphitic material, freestanding SCDms with improved crystalline quality were obtained. The SCDms were subsequently transferred to GaN, SiC, AlGaN, and AlN substrates without an adhesive layer. The successful formation of diamond/WBG and diamond/UWBG heterostructures demonstrates the feasibility of integrating the SCDms with a range of semiconductor platforms. Overall, these results establish hydrogen implantation as an effective route for producing high-quality SCDms for future diamond-based heterogeneous integration applications.

papers.title: Gate-defined quantum dot and charge noise analysis in a Forksheet transistor
papers.summary: We report the cryogenic characterization of a 14-nm nMOS Forksheet transistor down to 10 mK. We demonstrate that the device retains transistor operation with improved characteristics at cryogenic temperatures, while also forming a gate-defined quantum dot that can be tuned to the single-electron regime. In the quantum-dot regime, we perform low-frequency charge-noise measurements across different charge occupations and observe an average charge-noise amplitude of $\langle S_0\rangle = 10\;μ\mathrm{eV}/\sqrt{\mathrm{Hz}}$ at 1 Hz, with a minimum measured value of $3.3\;μ\mathrm{eV}/\sqrt{\mathrm{Hz}}$. These results highlight the potential of Forksheet technology for the monolithic cointegration of quantum and classical CMOS functionalities in future quantum processors.
